title: What do you guys use for assets? Looking for SuperCell-like 3D characters
author: mrkvicka02
selftext: Looking for an AI that can create characters based on textual description. Ideally reference images of other things in similar style. The style I am looking for is relatively simple characters like in clash royale, clash of clans or brawl stars. Secondly, what do you do for animations?

replies.author: mrkvicka02
replies.body: So I tried meshy today and the character itself seems fine. I just wish there was an easy way to create a family of assets that match in style. I feel like right now they are not matching perfectly. Is it good? I will need A LOT of assets for the backdrop too.

comments.author: Cristazio
comments.body: There are AI tools to make models, but they all more or less suck. Meshy, Tripo, Rodin and Trellis all come to mind and you can try them, but none of them AFAIK do a good enough job in creating characters well enough. I think Rodin has a new tool for making separate meshes but I've never tried it. There's also RetroDiffusion but it mainly creates low-poly/cube-like models, so not really supercell-like, but so far is the only one that I found good at making, rigging and animating 3D models.

comments.author: Nilo_Team
comments.body:
for clash / brawl stars style chars you can type the description on [nilo.io](http://nilo.io) or drop a ref pic of the style you want and gen it right in the browser. then auto-rig it (works on bipedal T-pose chars) so you're not hand-rigging before animating. model settings + LOD slider if you want them light for mobile, export GLB/FBX into your engine. free plan has weekly usage so you can test the style first

LMK :)

replies.author: Nilo_Team
replies.body: you can even use a video to make animations from...

comments.author: Limp_Bus3865
comments.body: the style is not in the model it is in the shader

replies.author: mrkvicka02
replies.body: I think it is a good bit of both :) But I agree that the shader is a big part of it.

comments.author: Entropydemic
comments.body:
I only made a few Ai 3d models with Tripo or Meshy. Meshy is more intuitive but more costly, Tripo is cheaper but, in every way.

Like if you give Meshy multiple images front/back/side it will make a nice model, but if you don't tell it to T-pose your model will basically be a statue. You can also rig it with an intuitive tool which can differentiate bones of monsters or humanoids.

Tripo automatically can add bones to your models, but... it's automatic. Still, it has a slider which allows you to make a custom poly count.

I KNOW there is a thread here about this specific subject though, and there are much better 3d Ai tools than these.
